title: Associations of adolescent social media use trajectories with spatial and verbal memory: a prospective cohort study
authors: Nagata JM, Wong JH, Kim KE, Nayak S, Li EJ, Richardson RA, Rauschecker AM, Sugrue L, Ganson KT, Piatkowski T, He J, Testa A

primary_models.name: Weighted multiple linear regression of Year 2 cognitive performance (LMT, RAVLT) on baseline-Year 2 social media time trajectory group, adjusted for baseline cognition and sociodemographic, mental health and non-social media screen time covariates
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 2 (p. 6); results text p. 5; interpreted in Discussion pp. 5-7 and Abstract
primary_models.design: Prospective longitudinal cohort, two-stage analysis. Stage 1: group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) of average daily social media hours across three waves (baseline 2016-2018, Year 1 2017-2019, Year 2 2018-2020) classified each participant into one of three trajectory groups. Stage 2: the trajectory group (spanning baseline to Year 2) is the IV and cognitive performance at Year 2 is the DV, with the respective baseline cognitive score entered as a covariate. One Year 2 outcome per participant; no repeated-measures DV and no time interaction. Note that the IV window overlaps the DV wave (Year 2 social media time is part of the trajectory).
primary_models.sample: ABCD Release 5.1. Of 11,962 baseline participants, excluded those missing Youth Screen Time Survey from baseline to Year 2 (n = 2333), cognition assessments at baseline and Year 2 (n = 1372), baseline mental health (n = 1) and baseline sociodemographics (n = 728), giving analytic N = 7528 (Figure S1; included vs excluded compared in Table S1, excluded more often racial/ethnic minority, lower income, lower parent education). Mean baseline age 10.0 years (SD 0.6); 48.9% (3617) female, 51.1% (3911) male. Race/ethnicity: 58.2% White (4350), 14.2% Black (1240), 18.1% Latino/Hispanic (1159), 5.3% Asian (455), 3.1% Native American (267), 1.1% other (57). Parent education college or more 85.3%. Counts unweighted; analyses weighted to the American Community Survey. The 'Research in context' panel states N = 7582, which conflicts with the 7528 used everywhere else.
primary_models.iv: Social media time trajectory group (3 categories) from GBTM. Underlying measure: ABCD Youth Screen Time Survey item for hours per day on social media (e.g., Instagram, Facebook, Twitter), reported separately for weekdays and weekends and combined as ([weekday x 5] + [weekend x 2])/7 hours/day, at baseline, Year 1 and Year 2. GBTM fit in Stata 18.0 'traj'; best model by BIC was a sex-adjusted three-group solution (one linear and two cubic trajectories; Table S2). Groups: no/very low use (reference; n = 4289, 54.7%; about 0.1 h/day by age 13; legend '+0.1 hours/day' change baseline to Year 2), low increasing use (n = 2822, 38.8%; about 0.8 h/day by age 13; '+0.8 hours/day'), high increasing use (n = 417, 6.4%; about 3.1 h/day by age 13; '+3.1 hours/day'). Dummy coded against the no/very low use group.
primary_models.dv: Four Year 2 cognitive scores from the ABCD neurocognitive battery: (1) Little Man Task (LMT) accuracy, proportion correct over 32 trials (0-1), visuospatial attention/mental rotation; Year 2 mean 0.7 (SD 0.2). (2) RAVLT Initial Learning Trials, total words recalled over five learning trials of a 15-word list (0-75); Year 2 mean 44.2 (SD 9.1). (3) RAVLT Retroactive Interference (short delay recall after distractor list), 0-15; Year 2 mean 9.7 (SD 2.7). (4) RAVLT Long Delay (30-min) recall, 0-15; Year 2 mean 9.1 (SD 2.9).

primary_models.equation: Cog_Y2[i] = b0 + b1*LowIncreasing[i] + b2*HighIncreasing[i] + b3*age + b4*sex + b5..*race_ethnicity + b..*income + b..*parent_ed + b..*CBCL_ADHD + b..*CBCL_depression + b..*nonSM_screen_time + b..*Cog_baseline[i] + b..*site + e[i], with no/very low use as the reference trajectory; weighted by ACS-based sampling weights. b1 and b2 are adjusted mean differences in the Year 2 score relative to the no/very low use group.
primary_models.estimation: Multiple linear regression in Stata (GBTM in Stata 18.0 'traj'; the regression software is not stated separately). ABCD sampling weights approximating the American Community Survey applied to all analyses. Site entered as a covariate; no random effects or family clustering described. Two-sided tests, alpha = 0.05; Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, with bold in Table 2 marking significance after correction. Sex-stratified descriptive cognitive scores are mentioned (Table S4, supplement not in the PDF) but no sex- or race-stratified regressions were run; limitations note small subgroup sizes prevented this. No interaction tests reported.

d_transformation.conversion_formula: Categorical (dummy-coded group) IV on continuous DV: d = B / SD_DV, i.e., adjusted mean difference between the trajectory group and the no/very low use reference divided by the DV SD; applied to B_lo and B_hi for the CI.
d_transformation.contrast_type: Trajectory group membership vs the no/very low social media use group (low increasing vs reference; high increasing vs reference); not a per-hour slope.
d_transformation.notes: SD_DV taken from Table 1 (p. 5) Year 2 cognitive performance measures for the full analytic sample (N = 7528): LMT accuracy 0.2, RAVLT Initial Learning Trials 9.1, RAVLT Retroactive Interference 2.7, RAVLT Long Delay 2.9. These are total-sample SDs, not pooled within-group SDs, and Table 1 notes weighted estimates, so d is approximate. The LMT SD is printed to one decimal (0.2) and B to two decimals, so derived d for LMT is coarse (e.g., -0.03/0.2 = -0.15). Because the model adjusts for the baseline score of the same test, B is a residualized (change-like) adjusted difference; dividing by the raw Year 2 SD gives a d on the outcome scale. SD_IV is not applicable (categorical IV).

extraction_flags: The IV is a 3-group trajectory from a group-based trajectory model (GBTM), not hours per day, so d = B / SD_DV is a group contrast. SD_DV values are the Year 2 total-sample SDs from Table 1 (LMT 0.2, RAVLT 9.1 / 2.7 / 2.9), not pooled within-group SDs. The LMT SD is printed to only one decimal, so its d is coarse. The model adjusts for the baseline score on the same test, so B is a residualized difference. The trajectory window (baseline to Year 2) overlaps the Year 2 outcome wave. The Research-in-context panel says N = 7582, which conflicts with the N = 7528 used everywhere else. The supplement (Tables S1-S4) is not bundled in the PDF, so it is unverified whether Table S4 contains any sex-stratified social media estimates; the text and limitations suggest it does not. Software for the regression stage is not stated separately (GBTM is Stata 18.0). All 8 Table 2 values were checked against the pdftotext extraction.json
